implement.summary: Result: NO owner-fencing defect reproduced on BASE_SHA d8e5db3e; the objective is already satisfied as behaviour, so apps/mobile/src/data/accountScope.ts was left unchanged (no invented fix). The deliverable is the new adversarial matrix apps/mobile/__tests__/w02OwnerFencingMatrix.test.ts (11 tests, one commit 6022b2c2) which switches the active account A->B and A->B->A while an analysis is paused at each stage and asserts, against a real owner-keyed SQLite db and a fake edge API: (1) no owner-scoped row is written under B (rowsOwnedBy over every owner_key table), (2) nothing of A's work is readable through the active-owner read paths while B is active and B's bearer is never sent for A's work, (3) restored A recovers the pending result through the SAME durable operation id / journal row. Stage -> fence exercised (INFERRED from code, VERIFIED by the matrix): capture: OriginalAnalysisExecution invalidation on owner change (apps/mobile/src/analysis/originalAnalysisOperations.ts dispose/assertCurrent) + prepare()'s owner-scoped capture lookup, and forDataOwner() (apps/mobile/src/data/transactions.ts) rejecting a stale DataOwnerContext around savePendingCapture (apps/mobile/src/data/repository.ts) — a switch before prepare yields DataOwnerChangedError, during the INSERT INTO analysis_logical_operations yields OriginalAnalysisHeldError, B's prepare of the same operation is refused (OriginalAnalysisHeldError), restored A prepares/runs the same OPERATION id; extraction: runOriginalCaptureAnalysis re-asserts the execution after extractImportedPoseSequence resolves, so no journal/shot row is written for B and A resumes the saved operation; settlement: runJournal release_pending/committed states + runCaptureAnalysis replay of a committed result — a switch during permit reservation leaves A a recoverable journal and B nothing; a switch between durable commit and publication withholds the result from B and A replays it under the same operation without a second reservation; sync: drainOutbox owner context + syncRuntime configured-generation check (apps/mobile/src/data/syncRuntime.ts) — a switch mid-upload writes no receipt for B and A finishes its own sync later; plus an owner-epoch primitive test that A->B->A yields a new generation (apps/mobile/src/data/accountScope.ts) so every context captured before the round trip is stale. AC2 therefore has proof exit_code=1: the matrix PASSES on BASE_SHA (11/11) and on HEAD (11/11) — it documents existing coverage per stage (header comment of the test file) rather than exposing a leak. implement.approach: Round 1's matrix (11 tests across capture, extraction, settlement, sync, epoch) was sound but passed unchanged on BASE_SHA, so it failed AC2. Round 2 kept that matrix as the per-stage coverage documentation and located a concrete defect inside the authorized write path apps/mobile/src/data/accountScope.ts: setActiveDataOwner() (base line 57) notified subscribers with `ownerListeners.forEach(listener => listener())`, so the first subscriber that threw aborted delivery and every subscriber registered after it never observed the switch. Every owner fence in the shipping app is subscription-based — capture.ts:757-761 aborts the native byte comparison via subscribeToDataOwner, AnalyzeScreen.tsx:2187 abandons the in-flight analysis via subscribeToDataOwner, OriginalAnalysisExecution (originalAnalysisOperations.ts) invalidates its lease via subscribeToDataOwner — so a starved fence lets in-flight work continue for the previous owner after A→B. Test first (commit 1fa6ee2b + prettier 2c96e49e): a new describe 'owner-change delivery' with (a) an extraction-stage probe: faulty subscriber registered first, an owner-only AbortController fence (modelled on capture.ts) and the execution lease registered after it, extraction held mid-flight, owner switched away from A → asserts the switch is applied, the throw surfaces, and BOTH later fences fire; then B sees no rows/results, no B bearer is used, A returns and completes the SAME operation id; (b) a primitive probe: three subscribers (two throwing) all run in order against the new snapshot, generation bumps once, first error rethrown once, a no-op re-set notifies nobody. Fix (commit 7c06c0b6): setActiveDataOwner() delegates to notifyOwnerListeners(), which iterates every listener, captures the first thrown error, and rethrows it after the last listener — 16 added lines, no exported signature change, no other file touched. Wired into shipping behaviour by construction: every existing subscribeToDataOwner caller (authStore sign-out/sign-in paths call setActiveDataOwner) now receives every switch.

residual_risks: The fix changes error surfacing order inside setActiveDataOwner(): when a subscriber throws, all remaining subscribers still run and the FIRST error is rethrown after the loop (base rethrew immediately and skipped the rest). Callers see the same exception type as before; only the set of notified subscribers grew. No shipping subscriber is known to throw (INFERRED from reading capture.ts, AnalyzeScreen.tsx, originalAnalysisOperations.ts, syncRuntime.ts, React useSyncExternalStore glue); the hardening protects the owner-only fences (camera byte-comparison abort capture.ts:757-761, Analyze abandon AnalyzeScreen.tsx:2187, OriginalAnalysisExecution.recheck) from being starved by an earlier faulty subscriber.

The extraction-stage delivery probe switches the data owner BEFORE clearing the API session to isolate the owner-subscription path; shipping sign-out (authStore.clearSyncedRuntime → setActiveDataOwner) does the reverse, where the execution lease is additionally invalidated through the API-session subscription. The owner-only fences (no API-session subscription) are the ones the probe protects.
